approachQuestion.prompt:
Alternating signal cables. A directed graph has red and blue edges. Starting at s, return the minimum number of edges needed to reach t with adjacent edges of different colors, or -1 if impossible. The first edge may have either color; s=t requires zero edges. Revisiting a vertex is allowed when the resulting walk obeys the color rule.

Input: read-only outgoing lists of (neighbor,color), IDs 0..V-1, 1 <= V <= 100000, 0 <= E <= 300000. No duplicate (source,destination,color) triples; self-loops are allowed, and both colors may join the same ordered pair. Every edge has unit length.

Example: edges=[(0,1,red),(0,2,red),(2,1,blue),(1,3,red)], s=0,t=3, output=3 using 0->2->1->3. Reaching 1 directly after red cannot be extended by another red.

options.text: Run BFS on states (vertex,lastColor), allowing only edges of the other color. Initialize both color states of s at distance zero so either first color is allowed, and keep a separate visited distance per state. Return the smaller reachable distance at t.
options.feedback: Future legal edges depend on the last color as well as the current vertex. Two states per vertex retain exactly that distinction, and unit-edge BFS finds a shortest valid walk.

options.text: Run BFS with a last-color field in each queue entry, but permanently mark a vertex visited after its first arrival regardless of color.
options.feedback: In the example, arrival at 1 after red blocks 1->3. A later arrival at 1 after blue permits it. Suppressing that second state loses the only valid route to 3.

options.text: Run ordinary shortest-path BFS on vertices without checking colors.
options.feedback: For edges=[(0,1,red),(1,2,red)], s=0,t=2, this returns 2 even though the only route uses consecutive red edges and the required result is -1.

options.text: Enumerate all simple paths in the expanded (vertex,lastColor) state graph and return the minimum length among valid target paths.
options.feedback: This is correct because a shortest state walk has no repeated state, but route enumeration can be exponential. BFS shares equivalent prefixes that end in the same state and avoids that unnecessary enumeration.

feedback.reason: A location is not a complete search state when the previous edge changes which next edges are legal.
details: Allocate two distance entries per vertex, initially -1. Set both entries of s to zero and enqueue both states. Pop a state and inspect its vertex’s outgoing list; allow only edges whose color differs from the stored last color. For an unvisited destination-color state, assign the parent distance plus one and enqueue it. Process the full queue. At t return the smaller nonnegative distance, or -1 if neither exists.

Arrival color is part of state: reaching the same vertex after red and blue enables different next edges. A single visited bit per vertex would wrongly discard one possibility. Two zero-distance source states permit either first color.

Initialize both color states of s at distance zero so either first color is allowed, and keep a separate visited distance per state. Return the smaller reachable distance at t.”: Future legal edges depend on the last color as well as the current vertex. Two states per vertex retain exactly that distinction, and unit-edge BFS finds a shortest valid walk.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze bfs-color-states. V counts original vertices and E colored directed edges. Initialize 2V distances and reserve a queue for 2V fixed-size states. Each original outgoing list is inspected once for each reached color state of its source. Constant-time array, color and indexed queue operations; no hashing, recursion, copying, shifting, or amortized growth. Return a scalar, excluding input and result from auxiliary space; include distances and queue.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard worst-case bound for the specified implementation.

options.text: O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space
O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space
O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Two states per vertex and bounded edge inspections keep the expanded traversal linear.
details: The option “O(V + E) time, O(V) auxiliary space” is tight: there are 2V states and at most two inspections per original edge, so the factor two does not change O(V+E). Distances and the reserved queue use O(V). The option “O(V + E) time, O(1) auxiliary space” omits them. The option “O(V(V + E)) time, O(V) auxiliary space” incorrectly starts a new traversal per state rather than sharing visited distances. The option “O(V + E) time, O(V + E) auxiliary space” assumes the expanded edges are materialized; the method reads original lists directly.
